modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On March 22, 1957: A United States Air Force aircraft disappears with all 67 people on board somewhere over the Pacific Ocean.
On March 22, 1993: The Intel Corporation ships the first Pentium chips (80586), featuring a 60 MHz clock speed, 100+ MIPS, and a 64 bit data path.
On March 22, 1934: In golf, the first Masters Tournament was held at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia, United States.
On March 22, 1896: Charilaos Vasilakos wins the first modern Olympic marathon race with a time of three hours and 18 minutes.
